question: At a posted or 85th-percentile speed of 60 mph, what advance placement distance does Table 2C-3 show for deceleration to an advisory speed of 30 mph?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For a posted or 85th-percentile speed of 60 mph, Table 2C-3 shows an advance placement distance of **275 feet** under Condition B (deceleration to a listed advisory speed of 30 mph). This value is a guideline that should be applied with engineering judgment, and it reflects an adjustment for a 250-foot sign legibility distance appropriate for an alignment warning symbol sign. Guidance (recommended): - Table 2C-3, in the 60 mph row under Condition B, lists distances of 570 ft (0 mph), 350 ft (10 mph), 325 ft (20 mph), **275 ft (30 mph)**, 200 ft (40 mph), and 100 ft (50 mph). - Per the table's footnotes, the Condition B distances "have been adjusted for a sign legibility distance of 250 feet," and "for Conditions A and B, warning signs with less than 6-inch legend or more than four words, a minimum of 100 feet should be added to the advance placement distance." - "Warning signs should be placed so that they provide an adequate PRT. The distances contained in Table 2C-3 should be applied with engineering judgment." Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 2C-3, where the 60 mph row under Condition B's 30-mph column reads "275 ft"; [Image 3] shows the same Table 2C-3 within Section 2C.04 (Placement of Warning Signs) with the identical 275 ft value at 60 mph / 30 mph advisory speed. Citations: - Table 2C-3 (p.152) - Section 2C.04 Guidance §804 (p.153) - Section 2C.04 Guidance §5 (p.152)
